Recognition of alternating groups by spectrum

results.title: Spectrum of a group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The spectrum $\pi_e(G)$ of a group $G$ is the set of orders of the elements of $G$, where an element of infinite order is assigned order $0$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 16.107 on recognition of alternating groups by spectrum
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: This proposition asserts that there is a natural number $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$, every finite group $G$ with the same spectrum (set of element orders) as the alternating group $A_n$ is isomorphic to $A_n$.

results.title: Large alternating groups are recognizable by spectrum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a natural number $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$, every finite group $G$ whose set of element orders equals that of the alternating group $A_n$ is isomorphic to $A_n$.

results.title: Spectrum of a group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The spectrum $\omega(G)$ of a group $G$ is the set of natural numbers that are orders of elements of $G$, where an element of infinite order is assigned order $0$.

results.title: Finite composition series
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $m$ a natural number. A sequence $s_0, s_1, \dots, s_m$ of subgroups of $G$ is a composition series of length $m$ if $s_0$ is the trivial subgroup, $s_m = G$, and for each $i < m$ the subgroup $s_i$ is a normal subgroup of $s_{i+1}$ and the quotient $s_{i+1}/s_i$ is a simple group.

results.title: Non-abelian factor of a chain of subgroups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group, let $s_0, s_1, \dots, s_m$ be subgroups of $G$, and let $i < m$. The $i$-th factor of the chain is non-abelian if $s_i \cap s_{i+1}$ is a normal subgroup of $s_{i+1}$ and the quotient group $s_{i+1}/(s_i \cap s_{i+1})$ is non-abelian, that is, it has elements $x, y$ with $xy \ne yx$. When $s_i \le s_{i+1}$, this quotient is $s_{i+1}/s_i$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 16.27 (statement)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every natural number $n$ and every finite group $G$ whose spectrum, the set of orders of its elements, equals the spectrum of the alternating group $A_n$, every composition series of $G$ has at most one non-abelian factor.

results.title: Groups isospectral to an alternating group (Kourovka Problem 16.27)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $G$ be a finite group whose spectrum, the set of orders of its elements, equals the spectrum of the alternating group $A_n$. Then every composition series of $G$ has at most one non-abelian factor.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 19.80 ($OC_7$-groups)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition, asked by W. J. Shi, that every $OC_7$-group, that is, every group whose set of element orders is exactly $\{1, 2, \dots, 7\}$ (such a group is periodic), is isomorphic to the alternating group $A_7$.

results.title: Groups with element orders $1$ to $7$ are isomorphic to $A_7$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every group, finite or infinite, whose set of element orders is exactly $\{1, 2, \dots, 7\}$ is isomorphic to the alternating group $A_7$. This answers Kourovka Problem 19.80 positively (Mamontov and Jabara).

results.title: Golod group (Kourovka 12.102)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $k$ be a field, $N$ a non-unital associative $k$-algebra and $y_1, \dots, y_r \in N$. The Golod group of $y$ is the subgroup of the group of units of the unitization $k \oplus N$ generated by the units that are equal to $1 + y_i$ for some $i$. When every $1 + y_i$ is invertible (for example when $N$ is nil), this is the subgroup $\langle 1 + y_1, \dots, 1 + y_r \rangle$ of the adjoint group $1 + N$.

path: Surjections injective on no nontrivial subgroup

results.title: Kourovka Problem 17.50: surjections injective on no nontrivial subgroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every finite group $G$ there are a finite group $F$ and a surjective homomorphism $f \colon F \to G$ such that for every nontrivial subgroup $H$ of $F$ the restriction of $f$ to $H$ is not injective.

results.title: Burichenko's theorem on surjections injective on no nontrivial subgroup
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite group $G$ there are a finite group $F$ and a surjective homomorphism $f \colon F \to G$ such that for every nontrivial subgroup $H$ of $F$ the restriction of $f$ to $H$ is not injective.

results.title: Alder's totient with second argument 2
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Alder's extension of Euler's totient with second argument $2$ is the arithmetic function $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ sending a natural number $k$ to the number of natural numbers $r < k$ with $\gcd(k, r) = 1$ and $\gcd(k, 2r+1) = 1$. In particular $g(0) = 0$, since there is no natural number $r < 0$.

results.title: Alder's totient at a successor as a count over an inclusive range
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $k$, Alder's totient $g$ with second argument $2$ satisfies that $g(k+1)$ is the number of natural numbers $r \le k$ with $\gcd(r, k+1) = 1$ and $\gcd(2r+1, k+1) = 1$.

results.title: Alder's totient with second argument $2$ is at most Euler's totient
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $k$, Alder's totient $g(k)$ with second argument $2$ is at most Euler's totient $\varphi(k)$.

results.title: Coprimality indicator of a graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $E$ be a set of ordered pairs $(i, j)$ of indices in $\{0, \dots, k-1\}$, the edge set of a graph $G$ on these $k$ vertices. For $n = (n_0, \dots, n_{k-1}) \in \mathbb{N}^k$, the coprimality indicator $\delta_G(n)$ is the natural number $1$ if $\gcd(n_i, n_j) = 1$ for every $(i, j) \in E$, and $0$ otherwise.

results.title: Coprimality indicator of the empty graph
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $G$ be the graph on $k$ vertices with no edges, and let $\delta_G$ be its coprimality indicator. Then $\delta_G(n) = 1$ for every $n = (n_0, \dots, n_{k-1}) \in \mathbb{N}^k$.

results.title: Coprimality indicator of a single edge: examples
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be the graph on the two vertices $0, 1$ with the single edge $(0, 1)$, with coprimality indicator $\delta_G$. Then $\delta_G(2, 3) = 1$ and $\delta_G(2, 4) = 0$.

results.title: Number of coprime pairs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n = (n_0, \dots, n_{k-1}) \in \mathbb{N}^k$, the number of coprime pairs of $n$ is the number of index pairs $(i, j)$ with $0 \le i < j < k$ and $\gcd(n_i, n_j) = 1$.

results.title: Number of coprime pairs: examples
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The triple $(2, 3, 4)$ has exactly two coprime pairs of components, and the triple $(6, 10, 15)$ has none, that is, its components are pairwise non-coprime.

results.title: Raw infinite q-Pochhammer product
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For complex numbers $a$ and $q$, the raw infinite q-Pochhammer product is the unconditional infinite product $\prod_{n=0}^{\infty} (1 - a q^n)$, defined for every $q$: when this product does not converge unconditionally (in particular for most $q$ with $|q| \ge 1$), its value is $1$ by convention.

results.title: Infinite q-Pochhammer symbol
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For complex numbers $a$ and $q$ with $|q| < 1$, the infinite q-Pochhammer symbol is $(a;q)_\infty = \prod_{n=0}^{\infty} (1 - a q^n)$, the unconditional infinite product of the factors $1 - a q^n$.

results.title: The q-Pochhammer symbol with a = 0
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$, $(0;q)_\infty = 1$, since every factor $1 - 0 \cdot q^n$ equals $1$.

results.title: Convergence of the infinite q-Pochhammer product
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all complex numbers $a$ and $q$ with $|q| < 1$, the infinite product $\prod_{n=0}^{\infty} (1 - a q^n)$ converges unconditionally to the infinite q-Pochhammer symbol $(a;q)_\infty$: the products of the factors $1 - a q^n$ over finite sets of indices $n$ tend to $(a;q)_\infty$.

results.title: The q-Pochhammer symbol vanishes at a = 1 and q = 0
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The infinite q-Pochhammer symbol satisfies $(1;0)_\infty = 0$, because its factor for $n = 0$ is $1 - 1 \cdot 0^0 = 0$ (with the convention $0^0 = 1$).

results.title: The raw q-Pochhammer product at a = 2 and q = 1 equals 1
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The raw infinite q-Pochhammer product at $a = 2$ and $q = 1$ equals $1$.

results.title: The Euler products of partition theory
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $k$, the Euler product $f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ is this infinite product in the ring of integer power series in $q$, taken in the coefficientwise topology. It is used for $k \ge 1$.

results.title: Pentagonal series expansion of the first Euler product
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Euler product $f_1 = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^m)$ equals the pentagonal series $\sum_{j \in \mathbb{Z}} (-1)^j q^{j(3j-1)/2}$ as an integer power series.

results.title: Constant term of the Euler products
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $k \ge 1$, the integer power series $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ has constant coefficient $1$.

results.summary: For a natural number $n$, $s(n)$ is the number of elements of the remainder set $S(n)$, that is, the number of distinct values of $n \bmod k$ for $1 \le k \le \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ (OEIS A283190).

results.title: The remainder count of 11
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The number $s(11)$ of distinct remainders $11 \bmod k$ for $1 \le k \le 5$ equals $4$.

results.title: The remainder count of 12
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The number $s(12)$ of distinct remainders $12 \bmod k$ for $1 \le k \le 6$ equals $2$.

results.title: The remainder-set constant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The remainder-set constant is $c = \sum_{p} \frac{1}{p(p+1)} \prod_{q < p} \left(1 - \frac{1}{q}\right)$, where $p$ runs over all primes and, for each $p$, $q$ runs over the primes less than $p$.

results.title: Asymptotic formula for the number of remainders
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $s(n)$ be the number of distinct remainders $n \bmod k$ with $1 \le k \le \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ and let $c$ be the remainder-set constant. Then, as $n \to \infty$ over the natural numbers, $s(n) - cn = O\bigl(n / (\log n \cdot \log \log n)\bigr)$, and $s(n)/n \to c$.

results.title: Unbounded drops in the number of remainders
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $s(n)$ be the number of distinct remainders $n \bmod k$ with $1 \le k \le \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$. For every natural number $M$ there are infinitely many $n$ with $s(n+1) + M \le s(n)$; equivalently, $\liminf_{n \to \infty} (s(n+1) - s(n)) = -\infty$.

results.title: Consecutive differences of the number of remainders
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $s(n)$ be the number of distinct remainders $n \bmod k$ with $1 \le k \le \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$. Then $s(n+1) \le s(n) + 1$ for every $n \ge 1$; there is a real constant $C$ with $s(n) - C \log \log n \le s(n+1)$ for all sufficiently large $n$; and for every natural number $M$ there are infinitely many $n$ with $s(n+1) + M \le s(n)$, that is, $\liminf_{n \to \infty} (s(n+1) - s(n)) = -\infty$.

results.title: Upper bound $1.3\, n / \log n$ for the prime-counting function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 2$, the number $\pi(n)$ of primes at most $n$ satisfies $\pi(n) \le 1.3\, n / \log n$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm.

results.title: Tail of the sum of inverse prime squares
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: As the natural number $n$ tends to infinity, the sum $\sum_{p > n,\ p \text{ prime}} 1/p^2$ of the inverse squares of the primes greater than $n$ is $O(1/(n \log n))$.

results.title: Iterated remainder sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the iterated remainder sets $S_j(n)$, $j \ge 0$, are defined by $S_0(n) = \{1, \dots, \lfloor n/2 \rfloor\}$ and, for $j \ge 0$, $S_{j+1}(n) = \{n \bmod k : k \in S_j(n),\ k \ne 0\}$.

results.title: The first iterated remainder set is the remainder set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the iterated remainder set $S_1(n)$ equals the remainder set $S(n) = \{n \bmod k : 1 \le k \le \lfloor n/2 \rfloor\}$.

results.title: Iterated remainder sets of 35
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The iterated remainder sets of $35$ satisfy $S_6(35) = \{0\}$ and $S_7(35) = \emptyset$.

results.title: Maximal Pierce length via iterated remainder sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 3$ and $t$ be natural numbers, let $P(n)$ be the maximal Pierce length of $n$ and let $S_j(n)$ be the iterated remainder sets of $n$. Then the following are equivalent: $P(n) = t + 1$; $S_t(n) = \{0\}$; $S_t(n)$ has exactly one element and $S_{t+j}(n) = \emptyset$ for every $j \ge 1$.

results.title: Number of partitions in a box
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $j, k, n \ge 0$ be integers. A partition of $n$ is a finite multiset of positive integers whose sum is $n$; the empty partition is the unique partition of $0$. Then $p(j, k, n)$ is the number of partitions of $n$ with at most $k$ parts, counted with multiplicity, each of which is at most $j$. In particular $p(j, k, 0) = 1$ for all $j$ and $k$, while $p(0, k, n) = p(j, 0, n) = 0$ for $n \ge 1$.

results.title: V-partition
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Let $n \ge 0$ be an integer. A partition $\lambda$ is a finite multiset of positive integers, and its weight $|\lambda|$ is the sum of its parts. A V-partition of weight $n$ is a triple $(c, \lambda, \mu)$ in which $c \ge 0$ is an integer, $\lambda$ and $\mu$ are partitions all of whose parts are at most $c$, and $c + |\lambda| + |\mu| = n$.

For a list with head $a$ and tail $\ell$, it is $x$ followed by the whole list if $x < a$; it is $a$ followed by the ordered insertion of $x$ into $\ell$ if $a < x$; and it is the list unchanged if $a = x$.

results.title: Inserting a present element into a strictly increasing list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Over a linearly ordered type, if every element of a list $\ell$ is smaller than every later element of $\ell$ and $x$ belongs to $\ell$, then the ordered insertion of $x$ into $\ell$ is $\ell$ itself.

results.title: RSA key
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A textbook RSA key consists of distinct primes $p$ and $q$ and natural numbers $e$ (the public exponent) and $d$ (the private exponent) such that $ed \equiv 1 \pmod{p - 1}$ and $ed \equiv 1 \pmod{q - 1}$.

results.title: RSA modulus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The modulus of an RSA key with primes $p$ and $q$ is $n = pq$.

results.title: RSA encryption
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an RSA key with modulus $n = pq$ and public exponent $e$, encryption is the map $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ given by $m \mapsto m^e$.

results.title: RSA decryption
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an RSA key with modulus $n = pq$ and private exponent $d$, decryption is the map $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ given by $c \mapsto c^d$.

results.title: Chinese remainder isomorphism for an RSA modulus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an RSA key with distinct primes $p$, $q$ and modulus $n = pq$, this is the ring isomorphism $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \cong \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ of the Chinese remainder theorem, sending $x$ to $(x \bmod p, x \bmod q)$.

results.title: Checking a power identity through the Chinese remainder theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let an RSA key have primes $p$ and $q$ and modulus $n$, let $k$ be a natural number and $x \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, and let $(x_p, x_q) \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ be the image of $x$ under the Chinese remainder isomorphism. If $x_p^k = x_p$ and $x_q^k = x_q$, then $x^k = x$.

results.title: RSA exponent identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an RSA key with modulus $n$ and exponents $e$ and $d$, every $x \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ satisfies $x^{ed} = x$.

results.title: Correctness of textbook RSA
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Decryption inverts encryption on every message, including messages that are not coprime to `n`.

results.title: RSA encryption is a bijection
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an RSA key with modulus $n = pq$ and public exponent $e$, the encryption map $m \mapsto m^e$ is a bijection from $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ to itself.

results.title: Correctness of textbook RSA on natural numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an RSA key with modulus $n = pq$ and exponents $e$, $d$, every natural number $m < n$ satisfies $(m^e \bmod n)^d \bmod n = m$.

results.title: RSA-CRT decryption
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $(p, q, e, d)$ be an RSA key with modulus $n = pq$. For natural numbers $d_p$, $d_q$ and $c \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, let $c_p$ and $c_q$ be the images of $c$ in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$. RSA-CRT decryption of $c$ with the exponents $d_p$ and $d_q$ is the element of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ that corresponds to the pair $(c_p^{d_p}, c_q^{d_q})$ under the Chinese remainder…

results.title: RSA-CRT decryption is correct
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(p, q, e, d)$ be an RSA key with modulus $n = pq$, and let $d_p, d_q \ge 1$ be natural numbers with $d_p \equiv d \pmod{p - 1}$ and $d_q \equiv d \pmod{q - 1}$. Then for every $c \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, RSA-CRT decryption of $c$ with the exponents $d_p$ and $d_q$ equals the RSA decryption $c^d$.

results.title: RSA-CRT decryption with the standard exponents
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(p, q, e, d)$ be an RSA key with modulus $n = pq$ in which both primes are odd, that is $p > 2$ and $q > 2$. Then for every $c \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, RSA-CRT decryption of $c$ with the exponents $d_p = d \bmod (p - 1)$ and $d_q = d \bmod (q - 1)$ equals the RSA decryption $c^d$.

results.title: RSA key from the totient condition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given distinct primes $p$ and $q$ and natural numbers $e$ and $d$ with $ed \equiv 1 \pmod{\varphi(pq)}$, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function, this is the RSA key with primes $p$ and $q$, public exponent $e$ and private exponent $d$. Its conditions $ed \equiv 1 \pmod{p - 1}$ and $ed \equiv 1 \pmod{q - 1}$ hold because $\varphi(pq) = (p - 1)(q - 1)$.

results.title: Per-locus f4 form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The per-locus `f4` form `x ↦ (x A - x B) * (x C - x D)` on frequency vectors `x : P → ℝ`.

results.title: Per-locus f2 form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The per-locus `f2` form `x ↦ (x A - x B) ^ 2`.

results.title: Per-locus f3 form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The per-locus `f3` form `x ↦ (x C - x A) * (x C - x B)`.

results.title: Per-locus f2 form as a special f4 form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f2Form A B = f4Form A B A B`.

results.title: Space spanned by the per-locus f-statistics
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The space `V_F` spanned by all per-locus f-statistics (all `f4Form`; `f2Form` and `f3Form` are special cases).

results.title: Every f4 form lies in the f-statistic space
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every `f4Form` lies in `V_F`.

results.title: Every f2 form lies in the f-statistic space
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every `f2Form` lies in `V_F`.

results.title: Every f3 form lies in the f-statistic space
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every `f3Form` lies in `V_F`.

results.title: f4 statistic as the integral of the f4 form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The `f4` statistic is the integral of the `f4` form of the frequency vector.

results.title: Integral of a linear combination of f2 forms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A linear combination of `f2` forms integrates to the same linear combination of `f2` statistics, for square-integrable frequencies.

results.title: Symmetry of the per-locus f2 form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f2Form` is symmetric.

results.title: Per-locus f2 form of a population with itself is zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f2Form A A = 0`.

results.title: Per-locus f3 form is symmetric in its sources
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f3Form` is symmetric in its last two arguments.

results.title: Per-locus f3 form vanishes when target equals first source
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f3Form C C B = 0`.

results.title: Polarization identity for the per-locus f4 form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f4Form` in terms of `f2Form`: the polarization identity behind `f4_eq_f2`.

results.title: Per-locus f2 form in terms of f3 forms with a base population
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f2Form` in terms of the `f3` forms with base `o`.

results.title: Linear independence of Patterson's f2 basis
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Patterson's `f2` basis: the forms `f2Form i j`, `i < j`, are linearly independent.

results.title: Patterson's f2 basis spans the f-statistic space
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Patterson's `f2` basis: the forms `f2Form i j`, `i < j`, span `V_F`, i.e. every f-statistic is a linear combination of the `f2 Pᵢ Pⱼ`, `i < j`.

results.title: Linear independence of Patterson's f3 basis
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Patterson's `f3` basis with base population `o`: the forms `f3Form o i j` with `i ≤ j`, `i ≠ o`, `j ≠ o` are linearly independent.

results.title: Patterson's f3 basis spans the f-statistic space
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Patterson's `f3` basis with base population `o`: the forms `f3Form o i j` with `i ≤ j`, `i ≠ o`, `j ≠ o` span `V_F`.

results.title: Dimension of the f-statistic space is n choose 2
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The f-statistics of `n` populations span a space of dimension `n choose 2`. (A linear order on the populations, used to index the `f2` basis, is chosen in the proof.)
